clue.text: My time to wear Ascot headgear, say

indicators.note: the hat is said to wear the time letter, so that letter sits inside the headgear

parts.note: Royal Ascot race-goers famously sport elaborate fancy hats

explanation.surface: Someone decides it is finally their moment to show off a flamboyant hat at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English horse-race meeting known for outlandish hats. 'say' marks the definition as one example of the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild surprise, interchangeable as interjections: 'My!' and 'Well I never!'

clue.text: I feel crap shaking, but not by this!

definitions.text: I feel crap shaking, but not by this!
definitions.note: someone shivering with cold would not be doing so beside a warm hearth

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A shivering, miserable person complains, adding they would not shiver sitting by a warm hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the anagram, and the picture of a cold person who would be warm at the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth with a fire warms you, so nobody shivers with cold beside it.

clue.text: We really worry cure is not working

indicators.note: 'not working' hides a signal: 'working' says the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Anxious patients fret that their treatment is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like part of 'not working', but it belongs to the fodder; 'working' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: People prone to excessive anxiety might fairly describe themselves as those who really worry.

clue.text: I'm excited as she's obscenely coarse

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of delight, like whoopee
an uncouth boor, a lout, from Swift's brutish creatures; used loosely for a coarse person

explanation.surface: Someone squeals with glee because a woman is being outrageously vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a whoop of joy; the other is the boorish creature of Gulliver's Travels, a by-word for a crude lout.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a cry of glee and the name for a crude, boorish person.

clue.text: Terrible-looking skin American covers over

indicators.note: skin and American together cover the letter for over, holding it within

parts.note: an animal's skin is its hide
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something ugly with an American hide wrapped round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts O inside HIDE + US. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horribly ugly is terrible to look at; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Contrary communist grasping chaps annoy

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
contrary means facing the other way, so the word for the communist runs backwards

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a type of communist
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A bloody-minded leftie holds some fellows and pesters them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' gives TORT and 'grasping' is the container signal; Trot is a common shortening for a Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to vex or harass them, a stronger form of annoying.

clue.text: Small boy grabbing a grub from leaves?

indicators.note: the small boy grabs the letter a, holding it inside

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A little lad snatches a caterpillar from the foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like an insect larva in the leaves, but it means food; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is slang for food, and a dish made of lettuce and other leaves is food from leaves.

clue.text: A cop shot, one involved in that, perhaps

definitions.text: A cop shot, one involved in that, perhaps
definitions.note: a person who shoots a police officer might well be a callous, conscienceless type

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A police officer has been shot, and the culprit may be a dangerous personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles A COP SHOT with I (one). The whole clue also describes the criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking conscience or empathy is the kind of person who might gun down a policeman.

clue.text: One visiting fat person with an estate?

indicators.note: one goes visiting inside the fat, ending up within it

parts.note: lard is pig fat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somebody calls on an overweight landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One visiting fat person' reads as a rude description of a guest; 'visiting' puts I inside LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landowner with a large country property is known by this title.

clue.text: I told of a hellish trip in Escort around noon

definitions.text: I told of a hellish trip

indicators.note: the escort is placed around the letter for noon

parts.note: a date is a companion or escort on an outing

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a nightmare journey in a Ford Escort at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escort' with its capital suggests the Ford car; it means a date. 'around' puts N inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian poet's Inferno narrates his own journey through Hell, so he told of a hellish trip.

clue.text: Total dry spells with no DTs can be hazy

indicators.note: the dry spells are left with none of the named letters

parts.note: periods with no rain at all are droughts
the letters D, T and S, read as the familiar abbreviation for delirium tremens

explanation.surface: An alcoholic's account of drying out without delirium tremens is understandably vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DTs' is meant as the drinker's shakes, but it names the letters D, T and S, which 'with no' removes from DROUGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough idea is an approximate or vague one, so the word can mean hazy.

clue.text: Line manager should give one this

definitions.text: Line manager should give one this

parts.words: Line manager should give one this
parts.note: a boss ought to give guidance; a line can also be a course or bearing

explanation.surface: A worker expects guidance from their immediate boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'line manager' sounds like an office supervisor; a line is also a course to follow, and a manager steers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both guidance from a manager and the course a line takes are this, so the boss provides it.

clue.text: Poor novel needs editing — it's very cheesy!

indicators.note: a text that needs editing must have its letters reworked into a better order

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that a bad novel is corny and in need of an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheesy' looks like a literary put-down; literally the answer is a cheese. 'Poor' is fodder, not a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian cow's-milk cheese is, quite literally, very cheesy.

clue.text: Look back and snuff it — one tends to do both!

indicators.note: back means the little word for look is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
to snuff it is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces and then expires, as elderly folk do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LO into OL. The definition is cryptic: an elderly person tends both to reminisce and, eventually, to die.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person tends to reminisce about the past and, eventually, to die.

clue.text: A right one upset drunks and toffs

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: upset in a down clue sense of overturned, so the word for drunks is turned backwards

parts.note: sots are drunkards

explanation.surface: A conservative upsets some boozers and some posh types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SOTS into STOS. A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for aristocrats, the word means upper-class people, which is what toffs are.

clue.text: New role taken on by board is all right

indicators.note: the board takes on the new role, holding it within

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over afresh

explanation.surface: A fresh position accepted by the directors is satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal and 'taken on by' the container signal; 'board' means a table, not directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable but not outstanding is all right, a near synonym.

clue.text: Tube of paintings knocked over by red American

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word for paintings goes backwards

parts.note: paintings are art
Che Guevara is the archetypal red, a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: Pictures on the London Underground are toppled by an American leftist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns ART into TRA. 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is the windpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the anatomical tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: The sort of shot one hopes for in a round?

definitions.text: The sort of shot one hopes for in a round?

parts.words: The sort of shot one hopes for in a round?
parts.note: a round suggests drinks at the bar, but it is a round of golf

explanation.surface: A drinker hopes for a particular shot when it is someone's round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' and 'round' suggest pub drinks; in golf a round is the eighteen holes and the dream shot sinks the ball from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Every golfer dreams of holing the ball with the tee shot during a round.

clue.text: A salute brings soldiers aboard Concord

indicators.note: the soldiers come aboard the salute, going inside it

parts.note: to greet is to salute
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A military salute brings troops aboard the supersonic airliner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concord' looks like Concorde the aircraft; it means harmony. 'aboard' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is harmony or accord between parties, which is what being of one mind means.

clue.text: Foreign character treated piles at work

indicators.note: treated means worked on, so the letters are put into new order

parts.note: a machine that is on is at work

explanation.surface: An overseas visitor had haemorrhoids seen to while on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign character' suggests a person from abroad; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet. 'treated' rearranges PILES.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Love husband taking down trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the note-taking word pockets the husband

parts.note: noting is taking down, as in writing notes

explanation.surface: A spouse is caught with his trousers down, a saucy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets, putting H inside NOTING. Love is zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis term for a score of zero, which is no points at all.

clue.text: One inspiring hotel to get in popular beer and lager at last

indicators.note: the hotel letter gets in among popular and beer, sitting between them

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
ale is beer
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of lager

explanation.surface: An encouraging figure brings a pub mood: popular ale and finally lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One inspiring' looks like a motivator; inspire also means breathe in. 'to get in' is the container signal and 'at last' takes R.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is literally to breathe in, and an asthmatic's device is used to breathe in medicine.

clue.text: Bad girl smuggling drug banned by law

indicators.note: the bad girl smuggles the drug, hiding it inside

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
gal is a girl
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A wayward girl smuggles narcotics that the law forbids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggling' is the container signal; E is the usual slang for an ecstasy tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden under statute is unlawful, which is exactly what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Men on the right of former PM and Sadiq Kahn?

indicators.note: the men are written to the right of the prime minister, after her name

parts.note: Theresa May was a UK prime minister
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A political line-up: troops to the right of Theresa May, alongside London's mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was British prime minister 2016-19. Sadiq Khan (spelt Kahn in the clue) is the mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadiq Khan is the elected civic leader of London, an example of this office.

clue.text: Two mothers, one runs a disorderly house

parts.note: the first of two words for mother, ma being a familiar name for one
dam is a mother, especially of animals

explanation.surface: A pair of mothers, one of whom keeps a chaotic home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two mothers' gives two synonyms: MA and DAM. A 'disorderly house' is a legal term for a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who keeps a brothel is the classic sense of this title.

clue.text: Dutch river boys seldom have gone across

indicators.note: the river's letters go across the two words, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: Lads rarely make the crossing of a waterway in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle 'boYS SELdom'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a river in the Netherlands, also spelt IJssel.

clue.text: Gassy valet with a kit for new treatment

indicators.note: the letters are put in for a new treatment, coming out rearranged

explanation.surface: A flatulent manservant gets a kit for new medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gassy' suggests wind; here it means chatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Gassy is informal for prone to empty chatter, so someone gassy chats on and on.

clue.text: When ancient Scot throws his last wobbler?

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the ancient Scot throws away his final letter

parts.note: the Picts were ancient inhabitants of Scotland

explanation.surface: An old Scotsman finally throws a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbler' looks like a tantrum (throwing a wobbly); it means something that wobbles, a jelly. 'throws his last' removes T from PICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury meat jelly wobbles, so it is a wobbler.

clue.text: Unfortunately, balding is crippling

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Losing one's hair, sadly, is devastating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' scrambles BALDING IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that incapacitates or severely impairs.

clue.text: Call fraud if last bit of money vanishes

indicators.note: the letter vanishes, being taken out of the word for fraud

parts.note: a phoney is a fraud or impostor

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of money

explanation.surface: A victim reports a scam when their remaining cash disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last bit of money' gives Y, which 'vanishes' removes from PHONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone up is to call them, synonyms in the telephoning sense.

clue.text: Fight with Hoskins about English and the French

indicators.note: the setter's word goes about the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so Hoskins gives me
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The setter gets into a brawl concerning the English and the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, standing for 'me'. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused scrum or brawl involving many people is a fight.

clue.text: Bird seen in grand, ancient coat of arms

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
ancient means old
a crest is a heraldic device, part of a coat of arms

explanation.surface: A bird appears on a magnificent, old heraldic shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like an adjective; it is G, slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny European songbird with a gold stripe on its head, hence its name.
